questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which rule applies during refraction of light?
options: Light bends only while passing from rarer to denser medium
Angle of refraction becomes greater than angle of incidence when light travels from denser to rarer medium
Light bends towards normal from denser to rarer medium
From rarer to denser, angle of incidence is smaller than angle of refraction
questions.explanation: When light goes from denser to rarer medium, it bends away from normal. So angle of refraction becomes greater.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Study the given ray diagram in the textbook and select the correct statement.
options: Medium 2 is denser and medium 1 is rarer
Speed of light in medium 2 is lesser than in medium 1
Speed of light is twice in medium 1 than in medium 2
Medium 1 is denser and medium 2 is rarer
questions.explanation: The ray bends away from the normal in medium 2. This shows medium 2 is rarer and medium 1 is denser.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In refraction through a glass slab, which labels are correct?
options: 1-angle of incidence, 2-angle of refraction, 3-lateral shift, 4-angle of emergence
1-angle of emergence, 2-angle of incidence, 3-lateral shift, 4-angle of refraction
1-angle of refraction, 2-angle of emergence, 3-lateral shift, 4-angle of incidence
1-lateral shift, 2-angle of refraction, 3-angle of incidence, 4-angle of emergence
questions.explanation: These are the normal labels in a glass slab diagram. They show incidence, refraction, lateral shift and emergence.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which result is obtained from refraction through a glass slab?
questions.explanation: In a parallel glass slab, incident angle equals emergent angle. Both are greater than the refraction angle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the value of critical angle of glass?
questions.explanation: The critical angle of glass is 42°. This is the angle used for total internal reflection in glass.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which instruments/processes does total internal reflection take place?
questions.explanation: Endoscope, mirage and optical fibre use total internal reflection. Light reflects inside instead of passing out.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: For dispersion through a prism, if green, violet and red light velocities are vg, vv and vr, which order is correct?
questions.explanation: In glass, red light travels fastest and violet slowest. So the order is vr > vg > vv.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Identify the image characteristics for the object kept in front of the lens shown in the textbook figure.
questions.explanation: A convex lens used as magnifying glass forms a virtual, erect and magnified image. This happens when the object is close to the lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement about concave and convex lenses is correct?
options: Concave lens forms a virtual, erect and diminished image
Convex lens always forms only real, inverted, diminished images
Concave lens forms a virtual, erect and magnified image
questions.explanation: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image. So the image is smaller and upright.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the correct understanding of eye problems and causes?
options: Cloudy eye lens causes colour blindness
Increased eye-lens focal length causes shortsightedness
Change in cornea surface shape can cause a defect in vision
Night blindness occurs due to weakness of cone cells
questions.explanation: Irregular cornea shape can bend light wrongly. This can cause a vision defect.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is refraction of light?
options: Bouncing back of light from a surface
Bending of light when it passes from one optical medium to another
Absorption of all light by black body
questions.explanation: Refraction is bending of light. It happens when light passes from one medium to another.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a denser medium in optics?
options: A medium where sound is absent
A medium that always reflects all light
A medium in which light travels slower
questions.explanation: In a denser medium, light travels slower. So it bends more toward the normal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a rarer medium in optics?
options: A medium made only of metal
A medium in which light travels faster
questions.explanation: In a rarer medium, light travels faster. Air is optically rarer than glass or water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the normal in a ray diagram?
options: A perpendicular line drawn at the point of incidence
questions.explanation: Normal is a perpendicular line at the point where light strikes. Angles are measured from this line.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is angle of incidence?
options: Angle between surface and prism base
Angle between emergent ray and surface only
Angle between incident ray and normal
Angle inside the eye lens only
questions.explanation: Angle of incidence is between incident ray and normal. It is measured before refraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is angle of refraction?
options: Angle between refracted ray and normal
Angle between incident ray and surface
questions.explanation: Angle of refraction is between refracted ray and normal. It is measured inside the second medium.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which law says incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in the same plane?
questions.explanation: The first law of refraction says three lines lie in one plane. They are incident ray, refracted ray and normal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does refractive index compare?
options: Speed of light in two media
questions.explanation: Refractive index compares speed of light in media. It shows how much light slows down.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is critical angle?
options: Angle at which light disappears in air
Angle of incidence in denser medium for which angle of refraction is 90°
questions.explanation: Critical angle occurs in denser medium. At this angle, refracted ray goes along the surface at 90°.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is total internal reflection?
options: Splitting of white light into colours
Complete reflection of light back into denser medium when incidence angle exceeds critical angle
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection is complete reflection inside denser medium. It happens when incidence angle is greater than critical angle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the two conditions for total internal reflection?
options: Light from rarer to denser and angle less than critical angle
Light from denser to rarer medium and incidence angle greater than critical angle
Light in same medium and angle zero
questions.explanation: For total internal reflection, light must go from denser to rarer medium. The angle must also be greater than critical angle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a diamond sparkle more than similarly shaped glass?
options: Its cut and total internal reflection return much light inside it
questions.explanation: Diamond reflects light many times inside it. Total internal reflection makes it sparkle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a mirage related to?
options: Total internal reflection in layers of air
questions.explanation: Mirage is caused by total internal reflection in air layers. It often appears on hot roads or deserts.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is optical fibre used for?
options: Transmitting light signals by total internal reflection
questions.explanation: Optical fibre carries light signals inside it. Light moves by repeated total internal reflection.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is optical fibre useful in telecommunication?
options: It can transmit data at very high rate through light signals
It measures the density of milk
questions.explanation: Optical fibre sends data using light. This allows very fast communication.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is total internal reflection used in endoscopy?
options: Optical fibres send light into internal organs without large incision
It heats the body with hot water
questions.explanation: Endoscopy uses optical fibres to send light inside the body. It helps doctors see organs without a large cut.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is dispersion of light?
options: Splitting of white light into different colours
questions.explanation: Dispersion means splitting white light into colours. A prism can show this.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What causes dispersion through a prism?
options: All colours have identical speed in glass
Different colours travel with different speeds in glass
questions.explanation: Different colours travel at different speeds in glass. So they bend differently and separate.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which colour bends least in a prism?
questions.explanation: Red light bends the least in a prism. It travels faster than violet in glass.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a rainbow?
options: A shadow of the Moon only
A circular colourful arc formed by sunlight and water droplets
questions.explanation: A rainbow is a colourful arc in the sky. It forms when sunlight passes through water droplets.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process is involved in rainbow formation?
options: Refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in water droplets
questions.explanation: Water droplets refract, disperse and internally reflect sunlight. These processes form a rainbow.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a lens?
options: A transparent medium with spherical surfaces used to bend light
questions.explanation: A lens is a transparent object with curved surfaces. It bends light to form images.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which lens converges parallel light rays?
questions.explanation: A convex lens brings parallel rays together. So it is called a converging lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which lens diverges parallel light rays?
questions.explanation: A concave lens spreads parallel rays apart. So it is called a diverging lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is optical centre of a lens?
options: Point in a lens through which light passes undeviated
questions.explanation: Optical centre is the point in a lens where light passes without bending. It is near the middle of the lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is principal focus of a convex lens?
options: Point where parallel rays converge after refraction
Point in front of cornea only
questions.explanation: A convex lens brings parallel rays to a point. That point is called principal focus.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is power of a lens?
options: Reciprocal of focal length in metres
questions.explanation: Power of lens is reciprocal of focal length in metres. So P = 1/f.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the unit of lens power?
questions.explanation: Dioptre is the unit of lens power. It is written as D.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which sign is used for a convex lens power?
questions.explanation: A convex lens has positive focal length. So its power is positive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which sign is used for a concave lens power?
questions.explanation: A concave lens has negative focal length. So its power is negative.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is accommodation of the eye?
options: Ability of eye lens to change focal length for near and far objects
questions.explanation: Accommodation means eye lens changes focal length. This helps us see near and far objects clearly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the near point of a normal human eye?
questions.explanation: Near point is the nearest point seen clearly. For normal eye, it is about 25 cm.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the far point of a normal human eye?
questions.explanation: Far point is the farthest point seen clearly. For normal eye, it is at infinity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering?
questions.explanation: Iris changes the size of pupil. This controls how much light enters the eye.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where is the image formed in the eye?
questions.explanation: The eye lens forms image on the retina. Retina receives the image.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which defect makes distant objects unclear but near objects clear?
questions.explanation: Myopia makes distant objects unclear. Near objects can still be seen clearly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which lens corrects shortsightedness?
questions.explanation: Concave lens spreads light rays before they enter the eye. It corrects shortsightedness.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which defect makes near objects unclear?
questions.explanation: Longsightedness makes near objects unclear. Distant objects are seen more clearly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which lens corrects longsightedness?
questions.explanation: Convex lens converges light rays before they enter the eye. It corrects longsightedness.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What causes night blindness according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency can cause night blindness. So vitamin A is important for vision.
